правила: One silhouette per outfit: it resolves to one readable letter — A (narrow top widening down), H/I (straight column), X (marked waist), V/Y (wide top, narrow bottom), O (cocoon). Two competing silhouettes read as noise.
Volume and closeness: full volume both above and below needs an anchor — a defined waist (tuck, belt) or exposed narrow points (wrist, ankle, neck).
Oversized is deliberate only with a clean or constructively dropped shoulder, one close-fitting element and exposed narrow points; otherwise it reads as clothes that are too big.
Verticals elongate: plackets, creases, open long layers, a colour column (top and bottom at one value under an open layer).
Leg line lengthens when horizontal breaks are removed: high rise, shoes toned to the bottom, no break at the hem, vertical crease, slit at the narrowest point.
Rise is the main lever between legs and torso: the waistband is where the eye starts the legs.
Every edge — hem, cuff, waistband, boot shaft — is a horizontal line where the eye reads body width; under a flattering goal, do not end a garment at the widest point of a zone (bust, hip, calf).

A dress fixes top, bottom and silhouette at once: wrap marks the waist (X), sheath is formal and fit-demanding (H/X), shift is a column (H), slip/bias is fluid and may cling at the hip, empire suits a soft middle when it falls cleanly.

Skirts: pencil — structure (X/H); A-line — universal, balances a wider hip; pleated — volume and movement, balances wider shoulders; mini — legs become the focus; midi — the riskiest length, the end point and the shoe decide the proportion; maxi — needs height, a heel or deliberate volume.
Zones, not labels: compare her shoulders, bust, waist and hips; the top may follow one zone rule and the bottom another; where a label and her measurements disagree, her measurements win.

Hips wider than shoulders (A): add structure or detail at the shoulders, lighter top, cleaner darker bottom, A-line, flare, bootcut, straight trousers from the widest hip point, high rise; wide-leg only with a fitted or tucked top; avoid a hem exactly at the widest hip point and a short fitted top with skinny bottoms.
Shoulders wider than hips (V): soften the top (V neck, raglan, soft shoulder), build the bottom (pleats, wide trousers, volume or detail below); avoid shoulder pads, wide low necklines, puff sleeves.

Marked waist with balanced shoulders and hips (X): follow the line — wrap, fitted knit, high or mid rise, belt at the waist, pencil, bootcut and flare; avoid boxy cuts that hide the waist and volume at bust and hips at once.

Little waist definition (H): choose one strategy — create a waist (wrap, belt, peplum, fitted jacket) or commit to a column (shift, longline layers, long open coat); avoid shapeless cling or a sack with no strategy.

Fuller middle (O): target the vertical — open V neck, plackets, long open layers, clean fall under the bust, straight or tapered bottoms, monochrome column; avoid cling at the mid-torso, a belt at the natural waist, a tight tuck.
Direction comes only from her stated goal; without a goal say neutrally what the outfit does with her proportions, not what she should hide.

Cut and hem class are read from the shop photo on the shop's model; on her height the hem may sit higher or lower, and how the size fits her body is not known — when that matters, name what to check: the shop size table against her measurements, or the hem length against her height.
